summary.text: Son of the infernal river Acheron who bore witness that Persephone ate the pomegranate seed, and whom Demeter crushed under a heavy rock in Hades — a wholly different Ascalaphus from the son of Ares who captained the Minyans at Troy.

story.text: When Zeus ordered Pluto to send Persephone up from the underworld, Apollodorus says, Pluto gave her a seed of a pomegranate to eat so that she might not tarry long with her mother. Not foreseeing the consequence she swallowed it — and because Ascalaphus, son of Acheron and Gorgyra, bore witness against her, Demeter laid a heavy rock on him in Hades.

Ovid tells the same betrayal with different parentage: Orphne, famed among Avernian nymphs, bore Ascalaphus to Acheron in an infernal cave; he alone saw Proserpina pluck seven grains from the pallid pomegranate rind, and with cruel lips debarred the Maid's return. The Queen of Erebus, indignant, made him a bird — the tale of witness and punishment that fixed Persephone's divided year.

The name is shared with Ascalaphus son of Ares and Astyoche, captain of the Orchomenian ships in the Iliad, whom Deïphobus slew before loud-voiced Ares knew his son had fallen. The atlas keeps them apart as `ascalaphus-minyan` and `ascalaphus-demeter`.
Son of the infernal river Acheron, crushed under a rock in Hades after witnessing the pomegranate — a chthonic witness, not a civic resident. Residence stays deferred.
